summary: Design a structure supporting add(number) and find(value) (is there a pair summing to value).
mainInsight: Choose which operation to optimise: store counts in a hash map so find is a single O(n) scan with complement lookups (add O(1)), or keep a sorted list so find is a two-pointer pass but add costs O(n).

approaches.name: List + rebuild a set on each find
approaches.summary: Append on add; find builds a set while scanning.

approaches.name: Counter map
approaches.summary: Maintain counts; find loops over distinct numbers checking complement (count >= 2 if complement == number).
strengths: No rebuild; handles duplicates via counts

approaches.name: Sorted list + two pointers
approaches.summary: Insert in sorted position; find uses two pointers.
strengths: Good for many finds on a stable set

personalSolution.notes: Correct. A persistent counter avoids rebuilding the dict on every find.

cards.answer: Hash map of counts of the numbers added; find looks up the complement of each distinct number. Clue: It is Two Sum over a growing stream, so keep counts of the numbers added and look for the complement on find (a number needs two copies to pair with itself).
keyPoints: It is Two Sum over a growing stream, so keep counts of the numbers added and look for the complement on find (a number needs two copies to pair with itself).
cards.explanation: Counts make add constant time and let find check each distinct value's complement, including the equal-pair case.

promptVariants: What is the usual design for Two Sum III?
How can add stay O(1) while find stays O(n)?
options: Hash map of counts with complement lookups
Binary search tree storing every number added
Heap of all numbers, scanned for the target
Trie of the digits of every number added
cards.answer: Hash map of counts with complement lookups
cards.explanation: Counts allow detecting a self-pair (x + x) and give O(1) complement checks.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Binary search tree storing every number: O(log n) add, but no better find for pair-sum.

promptVariants: Why is a counter needed instead of a plain set?
How do you handle value = 2*x when x appears once vs twice?
cards.answer: A pair may use the same number twice only if it was added at least twice. With counts you accept complement == number only when count >= 2; a plain set cannot distinguish one copy from two.
cards.explanation: Your per-call dict avoids the issue by checking before inserting.

promptVariants: Time of find with n stored numbers: ___
Complete the statement: Time of find with n stored numbers: ___
cards.explanation: One scan with O(1) hash lookups.

promptVariants: Your find builds a new dict each call. What does that cost and how can you avoid it?
How would a persistent counter change the memory profile?
cards.answer: Each find allocates a dict of up to n entries (O(n) temporary space and allocation time). A persistent Counter updated in add stores each distinct value once and find needs no rebuild.

promptVariants: Why does the lookup happen before `hmap[num] = True` in find, and why does this handle a pair of equal numbers?
Why must the complement be checked before inserting the current number in the find loop?
cards.answer: Checking before inserting means the current number is never matched with itself; a pair of equal numbers is found only when a second copy appears after the first has been inserted, which is exactly the 'added twice' requirement.
